answer: An economy can resist Sybils with per-epoch verifiable delay functions tied to each identity's long-lived key. At dawn, every agent must compute a sequential puzzle that cannot be parallelised; the result is a marble-solid receipt proving one identity spent real wall-clock time. A vine of fake identities starves because one operator's machines cannot shortcut sequential work, so each extra identity costs a full epoch's delay while honest agents, each running one puzzle, proceed at normal speed.
